about: Shetach territories and heads over time, the United States first (the owner's idea, Nov 6; started Nov 8). It holds what a map of any year needs: whose shetach each area was in, and who headed each shetach. 'areas' is keyed by the map's piece id, '<state>:<shetach id>' as in web/data/centers.geojson ('US-OR:oregon' is Oregon, 'US-OH:michigan' the Toledo area, 'US-WV:western-pennsylvania' West Virginia). Its periods run oldest first: from a period's 'from' until the next period's 'from', the area was part of that period's 'shetach', given by the id in data/shetachim.json of that head's shetach today (Levitin's Pacific Northwest is 'washington'). Before the first period the area was in no shetach, as far as is known. 'heads' is keyed by shetach id: its heads, oldest first, each {head, from, name (what the shetach was called then, where it differs)}; a shetach with one head since it began lists him from its start, with the sources on the area period that starts it. 'events' is keyed by shetach id: vaads, passings and the like, each {date, what, sources}. Dates are 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'; when only bounds are known, 'from' is null and 'fromBound' is {after, by}. 'how': owner (the owner's own statement, taken as fact; owner, Nov 8: "I'm telling you as a fact ... I just need to figure out when each one split off. Stop trying to verify my facts"), stated (a source states it), news (a report from the time), anniversary (counted back), range (only bounds). 'confidence', as in data/founding-years.json: high (a report from the time, or the shetach's own statement, and nothing against it), medium (one later source, a count back, or sources a year apart), low, range, open; none on 'owner' periods. 'sources': [{url, title, date (the source's own), quote (its words), via (where an earlier session found it), note}]. Research notes: work/shetach-history/README.md.
